**Status:** CONVERGING, 1.0.0.dev24 development candidate contract. The following interfaces are
implementation targets, not completed execution, performance or acceptance
claims. Historical dev10 comparison records remain bound to their original
source, wheel, numerical outputs and publication identities. No durable tests
or stabilization are assigned.

## SQLite workspace candidate (dev12)

The new CONVERGING workspace scope replaces the operation writer with one
stdlib SQLite database per Plan leaf at `operations/operations.sqlite3`, using
DELETE journaling and EXTRA synchronization. This is a target contract, not a
claim that the implementation or observations below have completed. Dev11
outputs remain historical evidence; the new goal does not rerun that writer or
its old-flow tests. Current operation stores use SQLite version6. Older databases or file-journal
stores fail with `UnsupportedEvidenceVersionError`: use a new Workspace and
recompute. Old data are neither migrated nor automatically deleted.

JAX Optimization defaults to `commit_every_generations=10`, a positive integer
excluding booleans. Explicit `None` remains invalid. Omission resolves after
backend selection: JAX uses 10, while explicit Julia retains its native value 1. Baseline
evidence stays in memory until the first complete group publishes it once. After N completed post-tell generations, one
transaction publishes their ordered numerical records and the latest full
CMA/RNG state. A short final group commits at the normal tail or a handleable
error; incomplete generation work is never presented as a resumable generation.
Checkpoint off retains evidence without fabricating a resumable snapshot. The
interval binds operation/task/checkpoint identity, not the numerical request,
so completed numeric cache lookup stays independent of commit granularity.
Explicit Julia intervals other than 1 are unsupported and fail before launch.
The workspace policy does not change numerical algorithms, precision, candidate
order or winner meaning. The dev13 sparse implementation below changes the
factorization mechanism under a distinct numerical algorithm identity.

A generation callback is delivered once per committed group, for its latest
committed generation, after commit acknowledgement and outside storage locks.
Intermediate generations do not receive deferred callbacks. There is no initial
baseline notification; the separate final completion callback remains. Original callback, numerical and
interruption errors remain primary if recording also fails. A transaction has a
unique identity: an uncertain commit is reconciled from that identity, never
blindly replayed. Canonical byte objects have content hashes; references identify
the object inside the database, not a hash of its changing database file.

Readonly `resolve`, Benchmark and public reopen never repair SQLite state.
`WorkspaceRecoveryRequiredError` directs callers to explicit
`run.recover_workspace()` when recovery is required. This method verifies the
Run’s bound Plan leaf and recovers only its existing operation store. An absent
operation database in a valid leaf is a no-op; recovery never creates a database
or migrates historical data. A hot journal requiring rollback raises this typed
error from readonly access rather than triggering an implicit repair. Operation/span
indexes support timeline reads without replaying all numerical candidates.
Existing clocks, result units/axes, partial provenance and rendering semantics
remain; no UI redesign or physical power-loss promise is introduced.

The earlier SQLite-workspace performance campaign's scope was 14 CPU1
current-disk tasks and four SSD tasks over LC and M80-fixed models. That matrix
and its version-bound observations are historical; they are not dev24 execution
or delivery obligations. The current architecture/lifecycle candidate uses only
its assigned stage-specific installed-wheel observations. No speed or numerical
acceptance threshold is added.

## Warm preparation, progress and evidence residency (dev24)

`run.warmup(view, spec, parameters=None)` prepares the exact current JAX
Plan/parameter/View topology and executable signatures for an existing Direct,
quantity or Optimization declaration. Omitted parameters use the Plan baseline.
It returns an immutable preparation summary; it does not solve a network, run
Newton, choose an Optimization winner, create a checkpoint or claim a stored
successful result. Repeating an exact signature reuses its prepared entry;
future parameter-dependent shapes remain lazy. Warm entries belong to the Run;
operation-local candidate state is released at operation end. Shared executable
references do not authorize clearing another Run's cache. Reachable objects and
Python/native allocators may retain RSS after references are released; RSS need
not immediately drop. Run-owned warmed executables remain available to that Run,
while candidate worker state and operation-local scratch have operation scope.

Within a continuation, each intermediate step owns its compiler, material,
realized View, sparse pattern and executable references only through preparation,
evaluation and observation of the synchronized result. That transient scope ends
before continuation recursion begins. Endpoint and generation state retain their
existing ownership; this release does not clear Run-owned warm holders. A shared
weak executable index does not extend the lifetime of an entry. Releasing these
references does not promise immediate allocator or RSS return.

`run.optimize(..., progress=True)` enables a transient display observer,
independently of the durable `on_progress` callback. After each complete JAX tell,
the display distinguishes completed generations from committed generations.
The built-in `population_evaluating` phase is set before ask, so pending
population work is visible without implying a completed or committed generation.
A memory-only baseline display update is not an initial durable callback.
Explicit Julia displays its existing native notification boundaries as staged
progress, with an unknown durable generation count until verified terminal
success publication. Only then does the display report saved generations; no
new native observer is introduced.
Display errors warn and disable that observer; original durable callback errors
remain fatal. `progress=False` disables display without changing the numerical
request, candidate order, commits or callback cadence.

Uncommitted complete-generation evidence uses Workspace-bound, operation-local
scratch with mode `0700`. The candidate cache retains light body references and
the TaskWriter stages body references, rather than duplicate full candidate
histories. This scratch is not a checkpoint, SQLite commit or recoverable result.
Atomic publication streams one scientific body at a time for a group of complete
post-tell generations and retains one complete latest CMA/RNG state. The write
transaction verifies each body and releases its full payload after checking.
Resume hydration follows verified references one block at a time; it does not
retain duplicate raw and hydrated history containers. The full ordered typed
public ledger remains available as a fixed lazy generation Sequence, with its
original candidate/winner semantics. Explicit iteration materializes requested values.
Normal and handled-error cleanup removes only the operation's own scratch;
unexpected process death can leave it behind. An explicit cadence such as
`commit_every_generations=100` keeps the same persistence semantics; the default
remains 10. Workspace schema remains version6, and older Workspaces are rejected
rather than adapted.

Numerical plots size rows and wrapped text from their displayed content;
parameters appear as rows rather than long annotations. Plotting consumes saved
results and performs no numerical solve. Benchmark rendering remains a separate
operation/timing presentation, and schematic work remains deferred. These are
CONVERGING implementation contracts, not memory, speed or completed-case claims.

## Public operations and runtime configuration

Normal `CircuitRun.solve`, `evaluate`, `optimize` and `resolve` select JAX CPU
with `precision="float64"` by default. The Run constructor defaults to `backend="jax", precision="float64"`. Their
keyword-only `backend=None` and `precision=None` inherit those Run defaults;
explicit per-call values override them, including `backend="julia"` and JAX
`precision="float32"`. Existing positional declarations, parameter ownership,
Views and typed result meanings remain. JAX runs in the calling Python process;
there is no Python numerical child, Julia discovery, Julia preflight or fallback.
Float32 uses real Float32/Complex64 kernel arrays, not rounded Float64 outputs.
Host SI declarations and CMA state remain binary64. Existing epsilon and
stagnation procedures derive from the selected kernel dtype; no new tolerance,
search envelope or numerical acceptance condition is introduced.

The dev14 JAX candidate covers Direct S/Y/Z, DiagonalRoot, ResponseElement,
OperatorElementRoot, HybridizedPole, S/Y/Z TransferZero,
ResidueNormalizedCoupling (diagonal or hybridized branches; fixed frequency or
complex-root midpoint), and Operator output. Public `evaluate`, parameter
sweeps and all existing scalar Optimization selectors/expressions share one
quantity authority across original, retained and transformed Views. Operator
matrices are inspectable outputs and cannot become scalar objectives. The
[Direct quantity contract](direct-poles-zeros-and-operators.qmd) owns the
formulas, certificates, units, baseline rules and denominator amendment; this
page does not introduce another numerical contract. Source-bound installed-wheel
observations for the new scope remain pending.

HB still requires explicit Julia. Explicit Julia retains its current Float64
contract and requires the optional Julia extra plus a manually provided Julia
executable; feature calls do not acquire Julia or automatically fall back.

`configure_runtime(*, cpu_threads: int | None = None) -> RuntimeConfiguration`
records an immutable process resource declaration. `None` leaves the existing
process resource default; an integer configures `PJRT_NPROC` before JAX CPU
initialization. Identical known declarations are idempotent. Changing a known
initialized configuration raises an actionable Kernel-restart error. The
implementation records externally initialized JAX honestly and cannot infer an
unobserved pool size. It does not alter process affinity, global JAX platform or
global x64 configuration. Per-call precision uses scoped dtype configuration.
JAX initialization itself stays lazy. Resource profiles use separate observer
Python interpreters; within each interpreter, normal operations run sequentially
and both precision choices can share the declared pool. This observer isolation
does not create a product numerical subprocess. The base installation requires Python
3.12 and the pinned CPU JAX/jaxlib and CMA dependencies; Julia remains optional.

Optimization retains generation checkpoints and boundary diagnostics. A JAX public
callback sees its event only after the corresponding group evidence is durable.
Native callbacks remain staged progress telemetry after the baseline checkpoint
ACK and do not promise per-generation durable publication;
callback exceptions and KeyboardInterrupt retain their original ownership.
Optimization accepts explicit checkpoint policy and exact checkpoint resume
references. Resume verifies the same request/backend/precision/resource/source
identity and policy. Checkpoint policy binds the operation/task/checkpoint, not the
numerical request hash: completed numerical results resolve independently of
generation/off. A cache-hit operation records its requested policy and actual
checkpoint availability without creating missing snapshots. Checkpoint off does
not discard numerical evidence or baseline/root
anchors. Standalone root anchors never become CMA-resumable checkpoints.

## Same-generation JAX Optimization resources

`configure_runtime(cpu_threads=N)` declares the task's CPU budget. Optimization
uses persistent candidate threads, with capacity bounded by N and the declared
population size. `None` retains coordinator serial execution with the existing
environment, and 1 is serial. The baseline is evaluated first and its actual
anchors are sealed by the coordinator. A global candidate-preparation barrier
precedes ordered objective/term waves. Candidates from another generation are
never submitted before the current generation is consumed.

Each candidate retains its own View, dependency and continuation state. Immutable
structure templates reuse topology and sparse index work within the operation;
physical validation, coefficients and current transformed-capacitance weights
remain candidate-specific. Dynamic sections are realized before selecting a
matching template. Transform declaration order and ordered numerical consumption
are unchanged. The coordinator alone owns CMA ask/tell and RNG, candidate mapping,
cache admission/registration, occurrence ordinals, cost aggregation, winner,
SQLite state and callbacks. Duplicate candidates share numerical bodies while
retaining their original ordered occurrences.

The fixed scheduler is `scnsim.candidate-thread-ready-batch.v1`. Its broker takes
a finite snapshot of compatible ready assembly requests after exclusive resource
acquisition, including requests queued while waiting for that permit. It does
not wait for the full population or pad missing candidates. JAX executes using
the shared parent PJRT pool and runtime coefficients/indices; exclusive ownership
is released before outputs or errors are delivered. Native sparse work then
shares the available budget through the fair gate.

For an integer CPU declaration, `threadpoolctl==3.7.0` establishes BLAS1 in the
coordinator and at worker initialization. Managed limits remain in force until
owned workers join, then prior library limits are restored. `None` leaves library
limits unchanged. The process resource lease also covers normal same-process
Direct/evaluate calls: integer declarations manage BLAS1 while retaining the
parent's declared PJRT pool. Read-only operations do not initialize numerical
resources. There is no executor selector, automatic fallback, Julia candidate
parallelism or process-affinity change. Runtime and checkpoint identities bind
the scheduler, source and resource declaration; resume must match.

The candidate scaling scope remains `CONVERGING`. Numerical algorithms,
precision, mesh policy, View replay and failure categories are unchanged. Only
existing typed candidate numerical failures become `Inf`; infrastructure and
worker failures remain fatal. On interruption, queued work is canceled, active
numerical work drains to its actual return, and owned workers join. Cleanup
errors are secondary to the original exception; there is no forced-termination
promise for a hung native call.

Numerical evidence remains complete and ordered. Commit grouping remains 10
complete post-tell generations by default. JAX baseline and sealed anchors stay
in memory: no separate baseline transaction, generation-0 checkpoint or initial
callback. The first completed group saves the necessary baseline body once.
Generation checkpointing saves the latest completed CMA/RNG and anchor restore
state; checkpoint off omits restore-only state. A complete tail uses the same
required acknowledgement-before-callback boundary. Optional timing is separate;
failed or uncertain required batches are not resent. Timing aggregates remain
`details.generation_performance` on the existing `population_evaluation` span.
Population average is wall time divided by population count, not individual
candidate latency. Preparation, permit wait, assembly and ordered collection
counters classify work without permanent per-candidate spans. Worker sums and
permit-held intervals are not CPU utilization or additive population-wall
components; overlapping work must not be summed into an exclusive total.
Necessary first-start imports, runtime discovery, pool initialization and
compilation are startup costs, not automatically redundant work or a universal
optimization target. Subsequent executable reuse does not imply Result-cache
reuse. This contract makes no universal speed or numerical-acceptance claim.

## One numerical and one result authority

PreparedAnalysis remains the immutable semantic declaration: sealed Plan,
selected View, Spec, effective parameter source and source-unit provenance.
Backend, precision and actual configured resource identity bind the canonical
request. Explicit Julia retains its native request/attempt/receipt verification;
JAX never claims a Julia runtime or native artifact identity.

The existing Python physical compiler, View realization, independent-job batch
scheduler, baseline continuation and CMA implementation supply the numerical
path. These implementations are reused, not translated into a second public
executor. Compiled JAX kernels are retained by executable signature, selected
dtype/device and resource initialization. They retain neither Plans, parameter
histories nor result documents. Shape preparation is the first observed
executable-signature preparation, not proof of uncached machine-code generation.
Different numeric requests with matching shapes can reuse kernels; verified
result-cache reuse remains a separate observation.

The Plan workspace leaf owns request/attempt/evidence/checkpoint and typed result
resolution. JAX numerical bodies are stored once with ordered occurrence and
artifact references. The JAX verifier checks real JAX evidence and feeds the
existing typed result constructors; it never fabricates a Julia VerifiedSuccess.
DirectSolveResult, DiagonalRootResult, DirectQuantityResult, OptimizationResult
and ParameterSweepResult keep their public quantity axes, units, detached-copy
ownership and plotting meaning. Reports and trace records reference numerical
authority rather than embedding another candidate history. `resolve` is read-only:
no runtime initialization, numerical launch, retry, cleanup or migration.

Numerical-result readback fixes a completion seal, exact attempt, reference root
and generation ancestry independently of diagnostic history. Construction verifies
necessary completion metadata, not all candidate bodies. The readonly ledger
Sequence and flat candidate discretization read selected indexed evidence in
short snapshots and return detached values, without capturing the Run or retaining
a growing body cache. History plots consume compact summaries; comparison takes
only baseline and exact best. Missing, corrupt or replaced evidence fails without
fallback or whole-history replay. The [Runtime lifecycle contract](../v1-runtime-contract.qmd#package-lifecycle)
owns the exact fixed-reader and materialization rules. Historical files retain
their execution identities but older operation Workspaces have no compatible reader.
Benchmark and recovery readers retain their separate diagnostic and checkpoint
responsibilities. This readback change does not change numerical requests,
cache selection, optimization order or winner semantics.

Explicit Julia operation traces link the actual verified native request,
canonical attempt SHA, receipt SHA, result SHA and attempt directory. The native
trace's `attempt_id` denotes that existing canonical attempt identity, rather
than a new benchmark UUID. Native task/environment IDs remain null because the
native authority does not define those records; `details.native_environment`
retains the actual executable, platform and Julia/BLAS facts available in the
verified attempt. Request facts survive preparation/execution failure without
inventing a completed attempt or result. Native child-clock alignment remains
unavailable unless actual clock evidence exists. Trace binding is published only
after the native coordinator releases its evidence ownership lock.

SQLite transactions own completed ordered evidence; snapshots contain CMA/RNG
state and references to the baseline/anchor and committed cache/history objects.
DELETE journaling with EXTRA synchronization uses SQLite’s commit and rollback
mechanisms, without promising survival of arbitrary physical power loss or
storage failure. An uncertain commit is reconciled by its unique transaction
identity; a selected or unknown delta is never blindly replayed. Uncommitted
objects do not establish a completed generation. Diagnostic persistence failures
must not mask a primary numerical, callback or interruption exception.

Grouped generation bodies reside in Workspace-bound operation-local scratch
until commit; cache and staged writer state retain light references. Publication
and verified resume hydration consume bodies one at a time. Increasing N can
increase uncommitted evidence and recomputation after process death: only the
latest committed full CMA/RNG snapshot is resumable, and an uncommitted tail is
unknown. Returning the complete typed ledger still requires its public result
representation; this policy is not a constant-RSS or bounded-result-size claim.
Normal completion or a handleable interruption flushes completed generations; a
SIGKILL cannot run that flush. SQLite object references identify canonical bytes
by role, length and hash within the relative database name, so relocation does
not require rewriting content references. Relocation must preserve the complete
Plan leaf, including SQLite journal state; readonly open performs no recovery.
Explicit Julia retains its existing native evidence files and verification
contract; this operation-store replacement does not rewrite native receipts.

## Current Workspace storage (dev22 CONVERGING)

OperationStore version6 retains DELETE/EXTRA and rejects older operation
Workspaces; use a new Workspace and recompute, without migration or deletion.
A verified-object cache lasts only one transaction or readonly snapshot and
includes role/length bindings; reopen/relock revalidates. Manifest plus operation
start publish atomically. Request/task/attempt/running state and operation
association register atomically. Canonical numerical bodies omit occurrence
context; occurrences preserve ordered task/key/source/cache/attempt facts and
reference that body. Hydration batches references within one verified snapshot.
No solver reads or background writer are introduced.

Normal solve/evaluate atomically commits result, attempt success and the first
selected success. One optional timing batch and separate final root follow that
required boundary; baseline diagnostics are not independently flushed.
Optimization diagnostics follow actual group ACK independently of callback
prerequisites. Numerical equations, dtype, candidate ordering, CMA and native
Julia baseline semantics are unchanged.

## Built-in read-only Benchmark

`run.benchmark(*, operations=None, method=None, backend=None, precision=None, status=None) -> BenchmarkResult` reads this
Run's current Plan leaf. Optional operation-ID and method/backend/precision/status filters select recorded
operations; omitted filters select all recorded operations in that leaf. A status
filter matches the independently recorded operation status **or** `task_status`.
The report preserves both facts: committed task success does not synthesize a
successful operation finalization, and diagnostic failure cannot hide that
committed numerical state. It does
not accept a Spec, backend arm, alternate workspace or launch controls. The old
public comparison executor is superseded. A returned `BenchmarkResult.workspace`
is the exact `<Plan leaf>/operations` directory containing `operations.sqlite3`,
not the enclosing Workspace root. `BenchmarkResult.open(benchmark.workspace)`
reads that same current version6 operation store without leaf discovery, recovery
or a root scan; older operation stores fail explicitly
and require a new Workspace and recomputation.

Every solve/evaluate/optimize operation has one root span beginning at the
method's first clock read. The root interval includes final Plan-writer
acquisition, Plan revalidation and pending diagnostic publication before its
endpoint; these finalization costs have no separate named phase row. Only the
final root append and return tail remain outside that endpoint. Large evidence,
checkpoint and diagnostic archival work stays inside the root; no child interval
extends past its root. Resolve and Benchmark remain fully
read-only and persist no spans.
`CircuitRun(..., timing="aggregate")` defaults to online grouped timing;
`solve/evaluate/optimize(..., timing=None)` inherits that setting, while explicit
`"aggregate"` or `"detailed"` overrides it. Diagnostic mode is absent from
numerical request/cache/checkpoint math identity. Detailed cache hits do not
recompute. Aggregates show count/status, inclusive sum/min/max and actual max
context; mean is derived on read. They cannot reconstruct a detailed Timeline.
Only detailed mode retains low-level actual intervals; known root/top-level
intervals remain truthful. Optimization keeps generation-only timing.

Actual nested intervals describe preparation, cache lookup, lowering/View, transfer,
executable preparation, synchronized numerical batches, sweep points and CMA
ask/tell/generations/checkpoint publication. Every span binds `operation_id`,
`span_id`, nullable `parent_span_id`, kind, clock, actual start/end and status.
A sweep operation can return a real mixed-outcome ParameterSweepResult: its
operation status describes completion of the public call, while each requested
point retains its own numerical success/failure. Operation success does not
assert every point succeeded. A single-point numerical failure still raises its
typed error; infrastructure failures remain fatal.
Ordered batch work is not assigned invented per-candidate durations. Numerical
outcomes and candidate occurrences carry references to their original evidence.
Trace buffering at generation/end follows the evidence barriers; callback
notification preserves durability-before-notify. Interrupted submissions and
terminated processes retain partial evidence; missing tails stay unknown.
Optional timing batches are stored once in independent operation timing streams,
never copied into numerical task events or measurement bodies. After their own
durable acknowledgement, the recorder releases acknowledged increments instead
of retaining and resubmitting the full history.
It retains the identity and active parent/clock state needed by subsequent
spans. Unacknowledged spans and the available failure tail remain pending under
the existing commit/reconciliation contract; an uncertain publication is not
treated as acknowledged. Archival does not discard persisted diagnostic data. Timing write failure stops
diagnostics for that operation, including optional root finalization writes,
independently of required numerical ACK and callback. An otherwise committed success returns with RuntimeWarning; required
commit/integrity/callback failures and real interruptions keep their ownership.
For a recorded failure/interruption, the public root's `details.failure` exposes
the exact saved failure record, including available type, kind, stage, message
and evidence. The reader does not infer a failure or result that was not saved.

The current process spans use one recorded monotonic clock per invocation.
Historical or Julia child intervals keep their actual clock and alignment
provenance; unknown starts/durations remain unknown. Parent/child intervals are
inclusive and may overlap. Cumulative operation duration is distinct from elapsed
wall span and must not be presented as summed nested work. JAX timings end only
after device completion is synchronized.

Benchmark JSON/HTML projects verified records without mutation. The timeline
places operation roots below their details and supports zoom, collapse and
cursor inspection, with counts and filters. It distinguishes complete, failed,
interrupted, cache-hit and historical/unaligned records; a partial report has no
fabricated winner or terminal numerical artifact. Report generation is not a
solver launch. Read-only aggregation does not create a recursive self-span.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  R[Public Run operation] --> P[Immutable prepared request]
  P --> J[Same-process JAX: compiler / View / batch / continuation / CMA]
  P --> U[Explicit Julia execution]
  J --> E[Plan-leaf verified numerical evidence and checkpoints]
  U --> E
  E --> T[Existing typed Results and read-only resolve]
  R --> S[Parented real clock spans: numerical refs only]
  S --> B[Read-only Run Benchmark timeline]
  E --> B
```

## Ownership and observations

Runtime owns public dispatch, configuration and semantic preparation. Numerical
execution owns lowering, dtype-local kernels, continuation and CMA scheduling.
Workspace owns durable evidence, trace publication, resume verification and
read-only typed decoding. Visualization owns timeline projection and rendering.
No report, kernel cache or trace creates a competing numerical authority.

The historical dev12 observation scope followed its own work packet:
Julia-blocked Direct/root/Optimization/sweep, grouped commit resume/tail/off and
callback/interruption ownership, actual SQLite capacity/transaction fault cases,
new/partial/relocated readonly projection and HTML inspection, and the 18 new
performance tasks described above. Unchanged dev11 observations are historical
evidence, not rerun or relabeled as dev12. The dev13 work packet separately assigns only its named functional observations.
No speed,
accuracy, memory, convergence or mesh Gate is implied. GPU, Windows Workspace,
Float16/mixed precision and additional quantity families are excluded.

## Sparse CPU numerical foundation (dev13 candidate)

The CONVERGING dev13 implementation replaces the JAX dense nodal path with
immutable indexed local stamps, candidate-specific sparse View congruences and
JAX numeric assembly followed by CPU CSC SuperLU. The source candidate now implements this path; installed-wheel observations
remain pending. There is
no selectable dense numerical fallback. Dense conductor, Port, selected Schur
and actual RHS blocks remain where the mathematics requires them; genuine fill
is preserved without dropping small values.

Compiler and View own binary64 SI lowering and declaration order. The backend
owns requested arithmetic precision, local frequency assembly, direct factors,
analytic derivatives and existing numerical certificates. C/K/G are coalesced
before their separate absolute bounds; each series-RL section is bounded before
section summation. For a realized section resistance that is exactly zero and nonzero
frequency, the dev20 CONVERGING candidate evaluates the same local equation
`(-i omega) (R - i omega L)^-1 = L^-1` as a constant inductive
stamp. The local inverse uses the selected actual arithmetic dtype and is
prepared once per realized section; its frequency derivative is exactly zero.
Width one uses the direct reciprocal; width two uses entrywise
mantissa/exponent determinant and adjugate-ratio evaluation in the actual
dtype, without global maximum normalization. Wider local blocks retain LU. One shared 2-by-2 determinant supplies both off-diagonal
entries without projecting or averaging the input matrix. Existing actual-dtype
residual, status and tolerance conditions remain unchanged.
The zero mask tests the realized binary64 section resistance after physical
section scaling and before casting to the backend arithmetic dtype; it is not
a test of the unscaled Plan resistance or a dtype-rounded zero.
Ordinary transpose, incidence weights, physical inputs and coalescing order
remain unchanged. Nonzero-resistance sections and the original zero-frequency
path retain their existing evaluation. This change does not alter root
conditions, add a tolerance or certify a previously failed candidate.
For retained, non-port-realizable Z transfer-zero only, the dev20 CONVERGING
candidate uses two-component expansions in the selected base dtype
(Float32/Complex64 or Float64/Complex128) through assembly and selected Schur
formation. The high/low sparse action uses one compiled JAX CSR row-batched core with
runtime coefficients, indices and RHS, ordered high/low traversal and masked
inactive rows. It preserves sparse structure without a dense operator or padded
stencil and replaces the former per-row Python dispatch. Transfer, compilation,
synchronized compute and download have separate diagnostic phases.
The high-part factorization is performed once and reused for one
fixed low-aware correction. Corrected-equation certification retains the pair
representation as its numerical authority. Consistently formed F/Fp are then
projected to declared-dtype Y/Yp for the current Z cofactor and denominator
calculation. Unconsumed H/Hp are omitted on this Z branch. Other Quantity
scopes retain their current arithmetic. Effective compensated coverage is
recorded explicitly; this is not a 128-bit-accuracy claim or a public mode.
Physical inputs, ordinary transpose, strict result/failure ownership, tau and
the 0.01 Hz condition remain unchanged. No mean estimate, fallback, automatic
precision change or new certification condition is selected.

Host continuation/CMA and Workspace commit/checkpoint
authorities remain separate. The private Python-to-Julia transport may materialize
a dense descriptor at that adapter boundary; explicit ordinary Julia is unchanged.

Runtime coefficients, indices and View weights are inputs, rather than captured
physical constants. Static-pattern preparation, compiled-kernel reuse and actual
call-local factor reuse are distinct observations. Installed-wheel functionality
remains pending; historical measurements
retain their original implementation identity.

The current JAX algorithm is
`scnsim.jax-sparse-csc-superlu-reuse-analytic-newton32.v1`. Canonical requests
bind it, and actual execution environment records bind SciPy and the selected
backend. This prevents an old dense request/checkpoint from becoming a new sparse
execution by relabeling. Historical files retain their original execution
identities, but current readers reject older operation Workspaces: use a new
Workspace and recompute, without migration or deletion. Current native Julia
result-file contracts remain unchanged.
Sparse assembly uses at most eight systems per chunk with an exact tail; each
system has a call-local CPU SuperLU factor reused for its actual RHS solves.
Retained roots factor only the eliminated block and form the selected Schur
operator and analytic derivative; they never invert the full singular root
operator. Timing distinguishes actual assembly, CSC construction, factorization,
RHS solves and checks; these nested intervals are not additive wall-time parts.

## Direct quantity extension (dev14 candidate)

The new quantity kernels reuse sparse JAX assembly and CPU SuperLU. Global and
eliminated operators remain sparse; local numerator/retained/output matrices
and actual RHS blocks may be dense. Native SuperLU denominator determinants
and analytic derivatives replace any requirement to reproduce handwritten
Julia pivots, under a distinct recorded JAX algorithm identity. Singular local
cofactor derivatives and the existing complete denominator solve residual
remain required. There is no performance, numerical agreement or new
convergence claim from this implementation description.

The host owns root continuation, coupling branch dependency order, scalar
projection and CMA; numerical adapters own local analytic quantity evaluation.
Typed Result decoding consumes verified numerical records and preserves actual
precision, units and axes without a Julia receipt. SQLite commits every ten
complete post-tell generations by default. The first committed group includes
the pending baseline body once; there is no standalone baseline commit or
initial callback. Callbacks follow required group ACK. Generation checkpoints
start at generation 1 and bind the latest completed state; off excludes
restore-only state. Native Julia retains its existing baseline protocol.

Coupling consumes two already-certified branch outcomes in declaration order;
it does not locate or polish those roots again. The shared quantity codec retains
actual scalar/vector/matrix dtype, including certified anchors restored on resume.
`DirectQuantityResult.evidence` supplements scalar fields with detached ordered
coordinate/channel bindings, certificates, hybridized null vectors and branch
evidence; it does not introduce child result identities or another solve. Loaded
operator arrays preserve `[frequency, row, column]` order, with the request grid
as their frequency authority. Native Julia algorithm identifiers remain unchanged;
JAX quantity and transitive Optimization identities distinguish this candidate.

The current request layer records per-family
`scnsim.jax.sparse_superlu.*` algorithm identities and the transitive
`direct_cmaes.cmaes_0_13_1.v2` identity. The numerical adapter separately records
its aggregate `scnsim.jax-sparse-csc-superlu-direct-quantities-newton32.v8`
identity, including the retained non-port-realizable Z transfer-zero
compensation scope described above; these layer identities need not be identical.
Other Quantity scopes retain their current arithmetic. The shared
selected-state factorization of the eliminated block Qee uses SuperLU
`MMD_AT_PLUS_A` structural ordering. One factor supplies both the Schur solve
and its analytic derivative solve. Other native factorization options, selected
arithmetic dtype, equations and eliminated-solve residual conditions remain
unchanged. The subsequent coupling reciprocity amendment below is a separate
numerical certificate change. This ordering is recorded by the new adapter identity; it introduces
no retry, alternate-order fallback, symmetrization or new tolerance. It does not
by itself establish full-model convergence or numerical agreement. The shared
`root_frequency_linewidth` projection converts certified complex omega into
public Hz fields. Certified quantities use dtype-preserving array records,
including scalar records, rather than a second persisted frequency result.

Optimization candidate records retain a canonical `dependencies` mapping from
content body ID to numerical quantity body. Objective terms carry `body_id`;
coupling evidence carries ordered role/binding/body references into the same
mapping. Public ledger rows preserve these joins without another result
artifact, solver call or storage lookup by the decoder. Sealed baseline anchors
reference certified bodies in the baseline authority and hydrate through the
same codec on resume. Standalone and sweep point rows retain their primary
quantity fields and the corresponding finished branch dependencies.

## Backend-aware compiler explanation (dev14 CONVERGING)

`CircuitRun.explain(ref, spec, *, parameters=None, backend=None, precision=None)`
inherits the Run backend and precision; explicit keywords override them. JAX
explanations use the existing sparse Python compiler and View realization at the
effective parameter point, including every ordered scalar objective View. Their
`scnsim.jax_preflight` evidence binds actual Plan/request hashes and declared
backend/precision, ordered original/transformed/selected/eliminated axes, sparse
COO coefficient and incidence records, local SeriesRL/Port blocks, resolved
physical fields and realized line grids. Host SI lowering is binary64; no
execution or numerical certificate is implied. There is no JAX initialization,
JIT, global dense C/K/G allocation, numerical solve or Julia discovery.

The existing ExplanationResult exposes the evidence and its line discretization
and HTML presentation. Sparse records explicitly identify their format and
shape; they are not native Julia dense compiler artifacts. Explicit Julia
explanations retain the existing compiler preflight. Compiled schematic
construction retains its separate native Julia authority.

## Selected-Schur reciprocity amendment (CONVERGING)

The JAX coupling reciprocity certificate accounts for the actual eliminated-solve
residual and arithmetic rounding when Schur cancellation amplifies raw skew. It
credits only the explained solve-residual contribution, preserving input-origin
asymmetry and the raw selected operator for every downstream quantity. Its
rounding envelope derives from selected dtype and operation counts, without an
empirical multiplier or an infinite overflowed success budget. The existing
eliminated-block checks run first; root, zero, residue, derivative and branch
independence conditions remain unchanged. There is no symmetrization, extra
solve/factorization, retry, fallback or mixed precision.

The [Direct quantity contract](direct-poles-zeros-and-operators.qmd) owns the
identity, corrected defect and evidence meaning. The aggregate v4
identity distinguishes this certificate from prior source-bound observations.
The shared helper records `raw_selected_matrix`, `raw_skew`,
`residual_contribution`, `corrected_defect`, `rounding_budget`, `allowance`,
`unit_roundoff`, `arithmetic_precision` and `input_skew`, alongside the raw
numerator/scale/ratio. Bound arithmetic rounds outward in the selected real
dtype, including operation-count-derived subnormal error terms. This
is a numerical reciprocity certificate within rounding uncertainty, not a
forward-accuracy, performance or complete-model convergence claim.
